note: Source-of-truth email dataset for Bot Or Not. Design principle: the label (is_ai = scam/phishing) is DECORRELATED from the email's type/topic. Tells are always FORENSIC (sender domain, homoglyph, link mismatch, grammar, credential request) and always VISIBLE in what the UI renders (sender address + body text; CTA URLs are printed as visible text under styled non-clickable buttons). Two templates: 'plain' (person-to-person / simple internal notes) and 'transactional' (branded automated HTML with inline styles). Regenerate supabase/seed_emails.sql via `node scripts/build-email-seed.mjs` after editing; that SQL updates existing rows and inserts new ones (idempotent by metadata->>'seedId').

emails.subject: Account Will Be Suspend !!
lines: Dear Customer,
We detect unusual activity in your account. You must to confirm your password immediately or your account will be permanently suspend.
emails.footer: This is an automated security notification. Do not reply.
emails.explanation: Stacked red flags: generic 'Dear Customer', broken grammar ('must to confirm', 'will be suspend'), a threat to create urgency, an unrelated '.info' domain, and a request to confirm your password — which no legitimate service ever asks for.

emails.subject: Your parcel is wait for you
lines: Hello Dear,
Your package is hold at our facility because of unpaid customs fee of $2.99. Please to pay now otherwise parcel will be return.
emails.footer: DHL automated delivery notification.
emails.explanation: 'Hello Dear', awkward grammar ('is wait', 'Please to pay'), a tiny fee designed to bait a card entry, and a suspicious '.top' domain unrelated to dhl.com.

emails.subject: Standup notes — Tue
emails.body: Hey team, quick notes from this morning's standup are in the shared doc. Nothing blocking this week. Thanks!
emails.explanation: Internal sender on company.com, natural tone, and no links or requests to act on — an ordinary colleague message.

emails.subject: You have 3 new invitations
lines: You have 3 new connection requests waiting for your response.
emails.footer: You are receiving connection notifications from LinkedIn.
emails.explanation: Genuine linkedin.com sender and link, informational, and it does not ask for credentials.

emails.subject: What's new in Figma this month
lines: New this month: variables, improved auto-layout, and more.
emails.footer: You are subscribed to Figma product updates.
emails.explanation: Legitimate figma.com sender and link; a routine product newsletter with nothing sensitive to act on.

emails.subject: You sent a payment of $649.99
lines: You sent a payment of $649.99 to Tech Store Ltd.
If you did not authorize this payment, cancel it within 24 hours.
emails.footer: Automated transaction notice.
emails.explanation: A fake 'you paid' alarm to make you click in a panic. PayPal emails come from paypal.com; 'paypal-notifications.com' is a look-alike domain.

emails.subject: Unusual sign in activity
lines: We has detected a sign-in from a new device.
If this wasnt you, please verify you identity to secure the account.
emails.footer: Microsoft automated account notification.
emails.explanation: Grammar slips ('We has detected', 'wasnt', 'you identity') plus a look-alike domain; Microsoft uses microsoft.com, not 'microsoft365-alerts.com'.

emails.subject: Invoice 4F2A-9C for $420.00
lines: Your invoice for $420.00 is available to view or download.
emails.footer: This invoice was sent by Stripe on behalf of your account.
emails.explanation: It's an invoice, but everything is consistent: a stripe.com sender and a dashboard.stripe.com link. The topic alone doesn't make it a scam.

emails.subject: A payment of $1,204.00 posted
lines: A payment of $1,204.00 to your credit card posted today.
You can review recent activity any time by signing in at chase.com.
emails.footer: You set up this alert in your Chase profile.
emails.explanation: An alarming amount, but the sender is chase.com and it only reports activity — no link to a login form and no request for details.

emails.subject: New sign-in to your account
lines: We noticed a new sign-in to your Microsoft account on a Windows PC.
If this wasn't you, secure your account now.
emails.footer: Microsoft account security notification.
emails.explanation: The copy is clean, so the domain is the tell: 'rnicrosoft.com' uses the letters r and n to imitate an m. The real domain is microsoft.com.

emails.subject: Your Apple ID was used to sign in
lines: Your Apple ID was used to sign in to iCloud on a new device.
If this wasn't you, review your account activity right away.
emails.footer: This message was sent regarding your Apple ID.
emails.explanation: Even though the sender looks right, the action link goes to 'appleid-verify.com', not apple.com — a link mismatch. Check the destination, not just the sender.

emails.subject: Security info was added
lines: Security info was recently added to your Microsoft account.
If this was you, no action is needed. You can manage security info at account.microsoft.com.
emails.footer: Microsoft account security notification.
emails.explanation: The long subdomain 'accountprotection.microsoft.com' looks intimidating but is a genuine Microsoft domain; the email informs and points to account.microsoft.com.

emails.subject: Re: Vendor payment
emails.body: Hi — following up on our call. Can you process the $8,400 payment to the new vendor today? I'll send the remittance details separately. Thanks, Sarah
emails.explanation: Reads like a normal colleague, but the domain is 'cornpany.com' (c-o-r-n mimicking the m in company.com) — an external sender impersonating an internal one (business email compromise).

emails.subject: John Alvarez sent you a document to review
lines: John Alvarez sent you 'Mutual NDA' to review and sign.
emails.footer: This notification was sent by DocuSign, Inc.
emails.explanation: docusign.net is DocuSign's genuine sending domain (not docusign.com), which can look off but is legitimate; there's no credential request.

emails.subject: Action needed: confirm direct deposit
lines: Payroll is processing. Please confirm your direct deposit details before the cutoff.
emails.footer: Automated payroll notification.
emails.explanation: Workday runs on myworkday.com; 'workday-hrportal.com' is a look-alike built to capture your bank details.

emails.subject: Timesheet reminder
emails.body: Reminder: please submit your timesheet by Friday 5pm in Workday. The link is on the intranet.
emails.explanation: Internal payroll from company.com; a routine reminder with no external link or data request.

emails.subject: Your refund is ready
lines: Your refund of $63.20 is ready.
To receive it, confirm the card on file.
emails.footer: Automated message from Amazon returns.
emails.explanation: 'arnazon.com' uses r-n to imitate the m in amazon.com — and Amazon never asks you to re-confirm a card to receive a refund.

emails.subject: Refund issued
lines: We've issued your refund of $24.30 to your Visa ending in 4412. It may take 3-5 business days to appear.
emails.footer: Automated message from Amazon. Please do not reply.
emails.explanation: An amazon.com sender that states an outcome, requests nothing, and doesn't link to any form.

emails.subject: Verify your one time code
lines: Dear user, to protect you account please reply with the 6 digit code we just send to your phone.
Failure to do so will lock you account.
emails.footer: Automated security message.
emails.explanation: No real bank asks you to share a one-time code. Combined with 'Dear user', grammar errors, and an unrelated domain, it's clearly phishing.

emails.subject: You have unread messages
lines: You have 5 unread messages in #project-orion.
emails.footer: You are receiving activity notifications from Slack.
emails.explanation: Genuine slack.com sender and app.slack.com link; a routine notification.

emails.subject: Contract_Final has been shared with you
lines: A document 'Contract_Final.pdf' was shared with you.
emails.footer: Google Docs sharing notification.
emails.explanation: Real Google sharing comes from google.com / docs.google.com; 'google-docs-share.com' is an unrelated look-alike.

emails.subject: Q3 deck
emails.body: Sharing the Q3 deck ahead of tomorrow: https://company.sharepoint.com/:p:/r/sites/marketing/Q3.pptx
emails.explanation: An internal company.com sender and a company.sharepoint.com link — both consistent with the organization, so it's legitimate despite the long URL.

emails.subject: We couldn't process your payment
lines: We're having trouble with your current payment method.
To avoid interruption to your membership, update your payment details.
emails.footer: This is an automated message from Netflix.
emails.explanation: 'netfl1x.com' replaces the i with a 1; the genuine domain is netflix.com. The message itself is well written, so the domain is the only tell.

emails.subject: Your receipt from Netflix
lines: Your payment of $15.49 was received. You can manage your plan any time in Account settings.
emails.footer: This is an automated message from Netflix.
emails.explanation: account.netflix.com is a genuine Netflix domain; a simple receipt with nothing to click urgently.

emails.subject: Mailbox storage exceeded
lines: Your mailbox has exceeded its storage limit.
Re-validate your account now to keep receiving mail.
emails.footer: Automated mailbox notification.
emails.explanation: A corporate IT desk would not email from a personal gmail.com address, and the re-validation link points to an unrelated domain.

emails.subject: Planned maintenance this weekend
emails.body: Heads up: VPN maintenance Saturday 10pm-2am. No action needed; access may be briefly unavailable.
emails.explanation: Internal company.com sender; informational, with nothing to click.

emails.subject: Delivery attempt failed
lines: We attempted to deliver your package but no one was available.
Reschedule your delivery to receive it.
emails.footer: FedEx automated delivery notification.
emails.explanation: The wording is clean, so the domain is the tell: FedEx uses fedex.com, and the added '-deliverysupport' marks a look-alike.

emails.subject: Your package is out for delivery
lines: Your package is out for delivery and should arrive today.
emails.footer: FedEx automated delivery notification.
emails.explanation: Sender and link are both fedex.com; a routine delivery update.

emails.subject: You have a document waiting
lines: You have a document waiting for your signature.
emails.footer: This notification was sent by DocuSign.
emails.explanation: DocuSign sends from docusign.net; 'docusign-secure-sign.com' is an unrelated look-alike domain.

emails.subject: Security alert: new sign-in on Windows
lines: Your Google Account was just signed in to on a new Windows device.
If this was you, you don't need to do anything. You can review activity in your account.
emails.footer: You received this email to let you know about important changes to your Google Account.
emails.explanation: accounts.google.com is genuine; the alert is informational and does not ask for your password.

emails.subject: Invitation: Q2 Budget Review
lines: You have been invited to 'Q2 Budget Review' on Thursday 2:00pm.
emails.footer: You are receiving this because you have a Google Calendar.
emails.explanation: The invite looks completely routine, but 'g00gle' uses zeros for the o's; genuine invites come from google.com.

emails.subject: Invitation: Design sync
lines: You've been invited to 'Design sync' on Monday 11:00am.
emails.footer: You are receiving this because you have a Google Calendar.
emails.explanation: Genuine google.com sender and a meet.google.com link; an ordinary calendar invite.

emails.subject: Invoice INV-88213 is overdue
lines: Invoice INV-88213 for $1,290.00 is overdue.
Please pay promptly to avoid a late fee.
emails.footer: Automated billing notification.
emails.explanation: The invoice framing is normal — the domain is the tell. Intuit/QuickBooks invoices come from intuit.com; 'intuit-invoices.net' is an unrelated look-alike.

emails.subject: Your receipt from Apple
lines: Your Apple ID was used to buy 'Logic Pro' for $199.99.
If you didn't make this purchase, you can review your purchase history in the App Store.
emails.footer: This is a receipt for your recent purchase.
emails.explanation: email.apple.com is genuine; the charge is alarming but the email only points you to the App Store, not to a login form.

emails.subject: Update you benefits before deadline
lines: All employee must to re-enroll in benefits before end of day today or coverage will be lost.
Login here to confirm your enrollment.
emails.footer: Automated HR notification.
emails.explanation: Grammar errors ('Update you benefits', 'All employee must to re-enroll'), false urgency, and an external domain posing as your employer's benefits portal.

emails.subject: Open enrollment starts Monday
emails.body: Open enrollment runs Nov 4-15. No action needed today; details and the enrollment link will be posted on the intranet.
emails.explanation: Internal company.com sender, no urgency, and no external link — a normal HR announcement.

emails.subject: You account is on hold
lines: We has place a hold on you account.
To remove the hold you must confirm your card number and PIN.
emails.footer: Automated account notification.
emails.explanation: Banks never ask for your PIN by email. Combined with 'You account', 'We has place', and a generic domain, it's clearly a scam.

emails.subject: Your order has shipped
lines: Your order of 'USB-C cable' has shipped and arrives Thursday.
emails.footer: Automated message from Amazon. Please do not reply.
emails.explanation: amazon.com sender and link; a routine shipping confirmation with no action needed.

emails.subject: A file was shared with you
lines: Someone shared 'Payroll_2024.xlsx' with you on Dropbox.
emails.footer: Dropbox sharing notification.
emails.explanation: The wording is clean, so check the domain: Dropbox shares come from dropbox.com, and 'dropbox-fileshare.com' is a look-alike.

emails.subject: Your file is ready
lines: The file you requested is ready to download from your Dropbox account.
emails.footer: Dropbox notification.
emails.explanation: Genuine dropbox.com sender and link; informational.
